rationale: Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲙⲟⲩϫⲧ̄ 'mingle, mix' with ⲝ for ϫ. Standard Manichaean cosmogonic verb for the entanglement of light and darkness. Qualitative form here ⲁϩⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄ 'has been mingled.'

Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲡⲥⲁ 'the side, region' with ⲍ for ⲥ orthographic variation, or possibly ⲡϩⲁ 'the place.' The phrase ⲡⲍⲁ ⲙ̄ⲡⲧⲟⲩⲱⲍ 'the place of dwelling' fits the cosmological context. Confidence low pending parallels.

Possible Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲱⲱⲧ (substantivization of ⲧⲱⲧ 'be joined, equal'). The phrase ⲛ̄ⲧⲟ̄ⲁⲧ ⲙ̄ⲡϣⲓ 'in the proportion of the measure' fits as a measurement-correspondence formula. Confidence low.
Standard Coptic verb 'be sufficient.' ⲛⲁⲣⲱϣⲉ ⲁⲣⲁⲩ = 'shall suffice for them' (3sg future + dative).

Greek loanword ἀριθμός 'number, count.' Used here in technical eschatological sense for the cosmic numbering of Days and hours. Distinct from Coptic ⲏⲡⲉ 'count, reckoning' which appears alongside in the formulaic 'count of the number.'
Lycopolitan compound ⲧⲁ-ⲛⲟⲩ-ⲛⲁⲩⲉ 'the (collective) of their hours.' ⲛⲁⲩⲉ = plural of ⲛⲁⲩ 'hour, moment' (cf. ⲡⲓⲛⲉⲩ in vocabulary). The ⲧⲁ- prefix forms a feminine collective.

proposed_english: the second of the Days / the Second Day
rationale: Standard ordinal ⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'second' + ⲛ̄ⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ 'of the Days.' Here designating the second of the eschatological 'three great Days' (cf. line 30 ⲡϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲟ̄ ⲛⲍⲟⲟⲩⲉ 'the three great Days'). Cosmological-eschatological technical term parallel to the cosmogonic Four Days/Four Nights schema.

Eschatological-cosmological technical term complementary to the three great Days. ⲡⲙⲟⲩ 'the death' + ⲥⲛⲉⲩ 'two.' Likely refers to two cosmic Deaths in the Manichaean schema — possibly (1) death of First Man's sons in primordial battle and (2) second cosmic death at end. Closes the chapter as paired counterpart to the Days.

Demonstrative ⲧⲁⲓ̈/ⲧⲫⲁⲓ 'this' + -ϯⲥ (possibly a substantivizing element) = 'this whole' or 'this totality.' Used here cosmologically of the entire system in which the cosmic events unfold. Cf. ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ 'the All' as semantically related but distinct technical term.
Lycopolitan demonstrative ⲡⲓ- + ⲣⲏⲧⲉ (= ϩⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'manner, fashion'). Discourse-comparative marker 'in this manner.'
Qualitative of ⲧⲁⲗⲟ 'mount, raise up, exalt.' Used here of the Light-Fathers being exalted in the new aeon — preserves the upward-soteriological semantics.
